titulo: Measure the session: medir-sessao.py, resume cost, and recall
lead: Without measuring, "the session got expensive" and "the agent forgot" are just impressions. The kit reads the JSONL transcripts from Claude Code and Codex and gives you duration, compactions, tokens and cache per turn, the real cost of resuming, and a search across everything that has been said. In this lesson you measure a known case and then your biggest session.
objetivo: measure the duration, compactions, tokens and cache of a session, read the cost of resuming, and find an old decision with recall.

aprende.t: Where the Claude and Codex transcripts live
recall: search in 0.02 s through everything that has been said

hero_alt: Bench oscilloscope showing a clean green wave, with probes on the table.

secoes.sub: Four kit tools, Python standard library only, no network.

nos.detalhe: One JSON line per event. They are not project source: half of it is tool output, they are deleted after cleanupPeriodDays, and Codex does not read Claude's. They are for measuring and searching.

Detects whether it is Claude or Codex and measures duration, compactions, turns, input and output tokens, cache (read ÷ input), bytes of tool output, and models. --json for machines, --por-turno for the curve. Reads 1.8 GB in ~9 s (measured on 10/01/2026).

Scans the Claude transcripts from the last N days (default 14) and compares (A) resending in a session of ≥ 150k that has been idle > 60 min with (B) a new session that starts with /prime. Unit: token-equivalents at the input price = input + 5 min write × 1.25 + 1 h write × 2 + read × 0.1.

Records the score on the test questions (lesson 5) by mode: compacted, resumed, continued, prime. --relatorio shows the hit rate and median context of each mode. It is the pair of the cost: one tells you what it cost to come back, the other how much came back.

It indexes what you and the agents said (no tool output) and searches by term, project, source, and date. Measured on 10/01/2026: 7,219 sessions became 90 thousand snippets, initial indexing took 1 min 24 s, incremental took 0.2 s, and a search took 0.02–0.04 s.

secoes.legenda: What was decided has to be in a file in the project. The transcript is for measuring and for remembering where to look.

secoes.titulo: Measure a known case, then your own
secoes.sub: The kit's test fixtures give fixed numbers: if your output matches, the tool is working right on your machine.

blocos.rot: Terminal · your biggest Claude Code session and the cost of resuming
blocos.conteudo:
S=$(ls -S ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl | head -1); echo "$S"
python3 ~/projetos/execucao-longa/tools/medir-sessao.py "$S"
python3 ~/projetos/execucao-longa/tools/custo-retomada.py 14
python3 ~/projetos/execucao-longa/tools/nota-retomada.py --relatorio

blocos.rot: Terminal · recall on the fixtures (separate index, in /tmp)
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/execucao-longa; R=/tmp/ensaio-recall
rm -rf $R && mkdir -p $R/codex/2026/10/01 $R/claude/-home-voce-projetos-demo $R/arq
cp $K/tests/fixtures/recall_codex.jsonl $R/codex/2026/10/01/rollout-a.jsonl
cp $K/tests/fixtures/recall_claude.jsonl $R/claude/-home-voce-projetos-demo/s1.jsonl
export RECALL_DB=$R/recall.db
python3 $K/tools/recall.py indexar --codex $R/codex --claude $R/claude --arquivo $R/arq
python3 $K/tools/recall.py indexar --codex $R/codex --claude $R/claude --arquivo $R/arq
python3 $K/tools/recall.py PostgreSQL
unset RECALL_DB

blocos.rot: Terminal · the real recall (once per machine, Linux)
blocos.conteudo:
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && ln -s ~/projetos/execucao-longa/tools/recall.py ~/.local/bin/recall
recall indexar                      # first time: indexes ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions
recall "cleanupPeriodDays" -n 5     # search (options: --projeto X --fonte codex|claude --desde AAAA-MM-DD)
cp ~/projetos/execucao-longa/tools/systemd/recall-indexar.* ~/.config/systemd/user/
sed -i "s#/home/nmaldaner#$HOME#g" ~/.config/systemd/user/recall-indexar.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now recall-indexar.timer   # reindexes every hour

secoes.titulo: How to read it and where to note it
secoes.sub: One line per run in progress.md, with the tool's numbers.

texto: Between 93% and 99% is the normal measured in long sessions. Much lower than that in a long session, look for pauses longer than the cache or a model switch midway.
Compaction does not drop the cache: it is no reason to cut the session short.
In Claude, compact_boundary lines; in Codex, compacted lines. Three in the same session: the hook has already asked for a new session at the end of the task (lesson 3).
To see when, use --json --por-turno and look for where the compactacoes column goes up.
It is not a limit: the big file does not block anything; what weighs is the context. But if it dominates, the agent is reading a whole log instead of tail -50.
On the final checkpoint line: input tokens / cache read / output and compactions, as the pilot did.
It is what lets you compare the next run with this one.

exercicios.titulo: E16 · The tool matches on your machine
exercicios.texto: Measure both fixtures and run the recall rehearsal.
exercicios.pronto: claude_mini → compactações: 1 | turnos: 2 and cache: 45.0%; codex_mini → cache: 60.0%; recall prints 2 arquivos processados; 8 trechos novos., then 0 arquivos processados and a line with PostgreSQL.

exercicios.titulo: E17 · Your biggest session in progress.md
exercicios.texto: Measure the biggest transcript from your Claude Code (or one from Codex in ~/.codex/sessions) and write the line in the progress.md of your run, with the date.
exercicios.pronto: the progress.md line has input tokens, cache read, output, and compactions equal to those medir-sessao.py printed for the same file.

exercicios.texto: Install the recall command, index, and look for a decision you remember making with the agent in the last week.
exercicios.pronto: recall indexar → N arquivos processados with N greater than 0, and recall "[termo]" --desde [data] returns the line with the file and the conversation line number.

perguntas.p: How does medir-sessao.py calculate the cache?
perguntas.explica: cache_ratio = cached ÷ input. In Claude, input is the sum of input + cache read + cache write, and cached is the read.

perguntas.p: Why is the JSONL transcript not a good source for what was decided?
opcoes: Half of it is tool output, it is deleted after the retention period, and Codex does not read Claude's
Because recall does not read it
It works, it's the best source
perguntas.explica: Decisions go in a project file (handoff, decisions.md, CLAUDE.md). The transcript is for measuring and for recall to find where to look.

opcoes: Resending in a big session with an expired cache × starting a new session with /prime
perguntas.explica: (A) first call after > 60 min idle with ≥ 150k × (B) a session that starts with /prime, in token-equivalents at the input price.

perguntas.p: Your session shows huge tool output. What does that indicate?
opcoes: That the file will freeze Claude
That the agent probably reads whole logs and outputs; ask for excerpts (tail) and write the log to a file
perguntas.explica: File size doesn't freeze anything; the active context is what weighs. Short tool output is one of the caps of every long run.

itens.texto: The fixtures give fixed numbers; if they match, the tool is right on your machine.
custo-retomada.py tells you how much it cost to come back; nota-retomada.py, how much came back.
recall finds where something was said; what counts is in the project file.
